column1: # Ledger kanji outside kanji_top1000.tsv, in the same columns and format.
# Only gives these ledger cards the Core Kanji layout; --seed-kanji never reads it.
# Readings, meanings, strokes and rank (KANJIDIC newspaper frequency, via kanji-data),
#   JLPT levels and WaniKani reading order: kanji-data by David Gouveia (MIT),
#   https://github.com/davidluzgouveia/kanji-data (commit 00fd707);
#   its KANJIDIC data is (c) EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0.
# Meanings are capped at 4; kun'yomi okurigana is shown as き(く).
# A leading * marks the most common on/kun reading (the one WaniKani
#   lists first among the kanji's readings); it is moved to the front of its list.
# Columns: rank, kanji, strokes, jlpt (N level, blank if none),
#   meanings (; separated), on'yomi (、 separated), kun'yomi (、 separated),
#   example (word|kana|gloss|JLPT level of the word, blank if none)
# Example words: the easiest word (JLPT N5 first, then N4 ... N1) that reads
#   this kanji with one of its on'yomi, the main on'yomi winning ties; if no
#   JLPT word fits, the most frequent common 2-3 kanji word in JMdict.
#   JLPT word levels and glosses: open-anki-jlpt-decks by Jamie Sinclair (MIT),
#   https://github.com/jamsinclair/open-anki-jlpt-decks (commit 1ad6673),
#   built from Jonathan Waller's JLPT lists (CC BY), https://www.tanos.co.uk/jlpt/
#   Other words and glosses: JMdict, (c) EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0 (2026-10-26),
#   https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project
#   Which kanji carries which reading: JmdictFurigana (CC BY-SA 4.0),
#   https://github.com/Doublevil/JmdictFurigana (2.3.1+2026-10-25).
